children: Malaysian palm oil futures snapped recent declines, with prices hovering near MYR 4,700 per tonne amid gains in rival edible oils and stronger crude oil prices.

Markets recovered from a two-week low, as exports remained firm, with cargo surveyors reporting a 46.9%–67.7% surge in shipments during Oct. 1–25 from the same period in Sept., partly driven by pre-Diwali buying in top consumer India.

Meanwhile, Malaysia’s Finance Ministry is reportedly reviewing a proposal to suspend crude palm oil export taxes as stockpiles hit a record in Sept. and are expected to top 3 million tonnes by year-end amid peak seasonal production.
However, contracts are on track to post their first weekly drop in four, down around 3% so far, weighed by ample inventories.
Timely rainfall between Sept. and Nov. also eased El Niño-related risks.
Still, futures are on track for a monthly gain of around 1.3%, after a 5.8% decline in Sept.
Traders now await China’s official PMI data for further demand signals.

title: Palm Oil Set for First Weekly Loss in Four, Monthly Gain Intact
